arguments.change_summary: Probe write: set preferred_jira_host on throwaway project PR-2011 to an inert placeholder URL to test PUT-vs-PATCH semantics on project settings.

attempts.note: First attempt succeeded immediately; no retries needed.

item_shape.project_settings: array of one single-key object per setting written, e.g. [{"preferred_jira_host": "<value>"}] — matches the declared write-response shape, which the contract explicitly notes DIFFERS from get_project_settings' single flattened object at element 0.

notes:
SETTING CHOSEN: preferred_jira_host (an inert Jira-site display/naming preference — no mail, no invites, no entitlement or retention impact) as the ONE setting changed, per instruction to avoid review/e-signature/timer/entitlement fields. review_approve was deliberately NOT touched: enabling it would gate later writes across the campaign, so per instruction I only note its presence in the body schema (Team Pro-gated, 422 otherwise) without invoking it.

PUT-VS-PATCH — SETTLED, CONFIRMED PARTIAL UPDATE (PATCH semantics), with a real (not just declared) two-step test: (1) baseline on PR-2011 was project_settings:[] (nothing stored). (2) Wrote ONLY preferred_jira_host → get_project_settings read back exactly {preferred_jira_host: "https://mcp-probe-test.atlassian.net"}, info.count=1. (3) Wrote a SECOND, different setting — tc_sharing:"true" — in a separate call that did NOT resend preferred_jira_host. The write response for step 3 echoed only {"tc_sharing":true} (one-object-per-setting-written, as declared). (4) Read all settings back again: {success:true, project_settings:[{"tc_sharing":true,"preferred_jira_host":"https://mcp-probe-test.atlassian.net"}], info:{count:2,...}}. preferred_jira_host SURVIVED a write that did not mention it. This is the strong version of the test (an empty baseline alone would have been inconclusive, since a single-key body trivially looks the same under PUT or PATCH when nothing pre-existed to wipe) — the second write proves omitted keys are preserved, not reset. VERDICT: this is genuine partial-update (PATCH-like, upsert-per-attribute-row) semantics, matching the capability's own documented guidance ('This is a partial update: only the keys you send are touched, and the others keep their stored values. It does NOT reset omitted settings.'). No disaster scenario observed: toggling one flag did not silently reset any others.

DRIFT FOUND — value typing contradicts documented guidance: the contract explicitly states 'Values are stored as strings in an EAV table, so send booleans as the strings \"true\"/\"false\"; that is also how they read back' and separately (on the read side) 'Every value is stored as a string ... booleans come back as \"true\"/\"false\"'. Observed reality: tc_sharing was sent as the string "true" but both the WRITE response ({"tc_sharing":true}) and the subsequent GET response ({"tc_sharing":true, ...}) returned it as a native JSON boolean, not the string "true". preferred_jira_host (a genuinely string-typed field) round-tripped correctly as a string, so this is specifically a boolean-vs-string coercion drift, not a blanket failure — the EAV-store 'everything is a string' claim in the guidance is false for at least this field. This is the basis for the DRIFT verdict.

CROSS-CAPABILITY PROJECT-SERIALIZER CHECK: not applicable here — neither the update_project_settings write response nor the get_project_settings read response embeds a project object of any kind (no data.project, no nested project fields at all); both are pure settings payloads ({success, project_settings[, info, meta_data]}). So this capability cannot be compared against create_root_folder's degraded embedded-project serializer or create_project's clean one — there is no third variant to report, because there is no embedded project object at all in this response family.

OTHER CROSS-CUTTING CHECKS: (a) Unfalsifiable settings blob — does NOT apply; the write body has 22 explicitly enumerated named settings (not a bare {type:object}), so DRIFT/PASS remains falsifiable. (b) Entitlement-gate-as-200-{success:false} — NOT exercised by this probe by design (review_approve and the two eligible-review-status fields, which carry the Team Pro gate, and part_11_reauth*, which carries the Enterprise gate, were deliberately never sent, to avoid gating later writes and per the explicit instruction not to enable review-approve). This probe therefore cannot confirm or refute that pattern for update_project_settings specifically; the sibling defect referenced in the campaign was observed on a different capability. (c) Error-envelope drift (3/11 declared shapes correct) — not exercised; both attempts here were clean 200s with no errors, so no error envelope was observed for this capability in this run. (d) No destructive or entitlement-changing field was touched; test_case_id_prefix, timer_*, part_11_*, and Jira/Azure allow-list fields were all left untouched. Final live state of PR-2011 after this probe: project_settings = {tc_sharing: true, preferred_jira_host: "https://mcp-probe-test.atlassian.net"} — left as-is since PR-2011 is expendable and no revert was requested.
